split.quote: The standard deduction for single taxpayers with adjusted gross income of less than twenty-five thousand five hundred dollars ($25,500) shall be three thousand dollars ($3,000).

notes: Both are fixed dollar amounts, with the standard deduction reduced by a fixed step schedule as AGI rises. Read in the official enrolled acts (SB19 and HB162 of 2022), not the live Code page (JS-only). Note the enacted AGI threshold is $25,500 (joint/HoH/single) and $12,750 (separate) while the dataset phase_out threshold reads 25999/12999 - possibly a modelling convention; worth a check. A 2025 bill (HB389) to raise the deduction was seen only as introduced; I did not confirm it failed.

index: Follows the federal standard deduction, i.e. whatever IRC 63(c) prescribes (itself inflation-adjusted federally under IRC 63(c)(4) by the IRC 1(f)(3) chained CPI-U method); DC adds no index of its own
base_year: n/a (federal; DC's older own COLA used the Washington-Baltimore CPI-U vs 2007 but applies only to tax years before 2018)

quote: (iv) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2017, the standard deduction as prescribed in section 63(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. [and] 'Internal Revenue Code of 1986' ... which provisions shall apply on the same dates that they are effective for federal tax purposes.
notes: Rolling conformity: DC standard deduction = federal 63(c) amount, so it moves with federal inflation indexing (and with any federal legislative change, e.g. 2025 federal increase). The additional 65+ amount is part of 63(c) (63(c)(1)(B), 63(f)), so it should follow the same way; DC text does not mention it separately. Dataset 15,000 single appears to be the pre-2025-federal-law figure; check whether DC conformed to the 2025 federal change (DC annually decouples via budget acts - not checked).

index: CPI-U (Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, US Dept of Labor)
base_year: calendar year 2011 (adjustment = $2,050 x percentage by which prior calendar year's CPI exceeds 2011 CPI)
rounding: rounded to the next lowest multiple of $25
schedule: Indexed basic amount defined only for taxable years ending on or before December 31, 2028; the statute is silent after that (not stated).
quote: (d-5) ... the cost-of-living adjustment for any calendar year and for taxable years ending prior to the end of the subsequent calendar year is equal to $2,050 times the percentage (if any) by which: (1) the Consumer Price Index for the preceding calendar year, exceeds (2) the Consumer Price Index for the calendar year 2011. ... If any cost-of-living adjustment is not a multiple of $25, that adjustment shall be rounded to the next lowest multiple of $25.
notes: Dependent/extra exemptions (204(c)) equal the basic amount so they follow the personal exemption. CPI is the average of the 12 months ending Aug 31. The IL Dept of Revenue lists $2,850 for 2025 and $2,925 for 2026 (https://tax.illinois.gov/questionsandanswers/851.html). Item (6) set a fixed $2,425 for TY ending 2023 (a one-off), so indexing was not continuous. After 2028 indexing is unstated in the current text.

quote: The pension exclusion is the lesser of the person's pension income or 'the maximum annual benefit under the Social Security Act computed under subsection (c)', less Social Security/RRB benefits received.
notes: The pension exclusion cap has no dollar figure in statute; it equals the Social Security maximum annual benefit at age 65 for the prior calendar year (the Social Security Act sets that amount with its wage-index/COLA rules), so it moves every year (nearest $100 allowed). The three other caps are fixed dollar amounts. The retired-ranger cap ($15,000, 10-209(e)) is also fixed but is not in this batch.

index: CPI-U (Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers), 'inflation factor' = CPI for June of the previous tax year divided by CPI for June 2023

So: indexed in 2025, flat 2026-2027, indexed again from 2028.

section: Mont. Code Ann. 15-30-2103(3) (as it stood for tax year 2025, struck by HB 337 Sec. 1 for 2026); 15-30-2101(12) 'inflation factor'; HB 337 (2025), Secs. 1, 2, 4-6

The pre-amendment text of (3) was read as the struck text in enrolled HB 337 (https://archive.legmt.gov/content/Sessions/69th/Contractor_index/CH0227.pdf), not as a live page, since mca.legmt.gov now shows only the 2026 temporary and 2027 versions. 'Inflation factor' defined at https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/title_0150/chapter_0300/part_0210/section_0010/0150-0300-0210-0010.html (CPI-U, June of previous tax year over June 2023).
